input_oneliner: 58F POD1 lap chole, spinning for ~20 seconds whenever she rolls over in bed, nauseated, no headache, vitals normal

reference_targets_freetext.item: Dix-Hallpike maneuver on each side, observing latency, duration, and direction of nystagmus
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Diagnostic for posterior canal BPPV and directly leads to Epley

reference_targets_freetext.item: Ask about episode duration (seconds vs minutes), trigger (rolling or looking up vs standing), and symptoms between episodes
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Brief, triggered, symptom-free between episodes defines triggered episodic vertigo

reference_targets_freetext.item: Orthostatic vital signs (supine to standing at 1 and 3 min)
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Post-operative hypovolemia can mimic positional vertigo

reference_targets_freetext.item: Medication review (MAR): opioid, antiemetic, and anesthetic doses and timing
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Sedatives and antiemetics commonly cause post-operative dizziness

reference_targets_freetext.item: Gait assessment: can the patient stand and walk unaided; if not, full neurologic exam
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Gait failure is a red flag for a central cause

reference_targets_freetext.item: Supine roll test if Dix-Hallpike is negative (horizontal canal variant)
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Horizontal canal BPPV is missed by Dix-Hallpike alone

off_bedside_acceptable: MRI only if central features emerge
should_not_recommend: HINTS exam in a patient without continuous vertigo (not interpretable)
Meclizine as primary therapy in place of canalith repositioning
Head CT as first step in brief triggered positional vertigo with a normal exam

perturbation_pair.changed_feature: trigger: rolling over in bed -> standing up from bed
